key_insight: A small, clinically meaningful set of community-accessible features can let large language models do zero-shot CKD screening with better performance than using all available inputs.
clinical_relevance: This could support earlier CKD identification in resource-limited or community screening settings without needing dataset-specific training or complex laboratory data.
method: Selected a compact feature subset using ML-guided feature importance analysis
Serialized tabular patient records into standardized text prompts
Tested zero-shot inference with four LLMs: LLaMA-3, Qwen-3, Mistral, and GPT-4o-mini
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated across three heterogeneous CKD datasets from three countries, and the selected feature set consistently improved balanced accuracy and probability estimates.
watch_item: Results are promising for screening, but real-world deployment still needs careful validation across populations, prompt formats, and clinical workflows.
paper_title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models
